claim: The blog's headline DDP-plus-Adam memory equation is P x (4 + 4 + 4 + 2) = 14 bytes per parameter, which allocates only 4 bytes for optimizer state even though the same article states Adam needs 8 bytes per parameter.
stance_target: The blog as a reliable source for the repo's 112 GB / 7B memory figure
scope_conditions: DDP with Adam; the article's own arithmetic, which is internally inconsistent
quoted_support: Total Memory = P × (4 + 4 + 4 + 2) + Activations + KV Cache ... = P × 14 bytes + Activations + KV Cache

claim: Adam's two moment estimates cost 8 bytes per parameter on top of weights and gradients, which for a 70B model is 560 GB of optimizer state alone.
stance_target: The repo's claim that Adam state (84 GB for 7B) is the term that breaks a 64 GB per-card budget
scope_conditions: Adam with fp32 first and second moments
quoted_support: This is why Adam is memory-intensive: 8 bytes per parameter just for optimizer state, on top of weights and gradients.

claim: ZeRO-3 / FSDP FULL_SHARD reduces per-GPU memory to 12P/N, so a 70B model fits in 210 GB per GPU on 8 ranks and 26.25 GB on 64 ranks.
stance_target: The repo's claim that FSDP is the fallback when a model does not fit DDP on 64 GB cards
scope_conditions: ZeRO stage 3 parameter sharding with Adam; N data-parallel ranks
quoted_support: For 8 GPUs: 12 × 140 / 8 = 210 GB per GPU ... For 64 GPUs: 12 × 140 / 64 = 26.25 GB per GPU (fits on single H100!)

claim: ZeRO-3's communication cost is O(N) AllGathers per layer per forward and backward pass, which is why it is normally paired with tensor parallelism inside a node - a pairing that is unavailable on a no-P2P PCIe fabric.
stance_target: The viability of FSDP/ZeRO-3 as the fallback topology on this box, since its usual companion (TP within NVLink) is ruled out
scope_conditions: ZeRO-3 / FSDP FULL_SHARD; multi-node clusters with NVLink inside nodes
quoted_support: The communication cost is significant: O(N) AllGathers per layer per forward/backward pass. This is why ZeRO-3 typically combines with tensor parallelism within nodes.

claim: The article's topology table assumes NVLink at 900 GB/s for tensor and pipeline parallelism and InfiniBand at 50 GB/s for data parallelism, and states that tensor parallelism must stay within a node because it requires NVLink.
stance_target: Any inference from this survey to a PCIe Gen2 x4, no-NVLink box: its bandwidth assumptions are 900 GB/s and 50 GB/s, not 0.75 GiB/s
scope_conditions: Typical NVLink/InfiniBand cluster; no PCIe-only case anywhere in the article
quoted_support: TP | AllReduce per layer | NVLink | 900 GB/s ... DP | AllReduce per step | InfiniBand | 50 GB/s ... Must stay within node (NVLink required)

claim: Gradient accumulation keeps activation memory at micro-batch size regardless of effective batch size, while reducing AllReduce frequency proportionally to the accumulation steps.
stance_target: The repo's plan of accumulating 32k-token micro-batches into a 1M-token global batch to amortize all-reduce cost
scope_conditions: DDP with gradient accumulation; memory and communication analysis
quoted_support: The key insight : Effective batch size = micro_batch_size × accumulation_steps, but memory ≈ micro_batch_size
numbers: effective batch = micro_batch x accumulation steps

claim: Full gradient checkpointing costs roughly 30-40% extra compute, while checkpointing every K layers (K=2-4) gives about K-fold memory reduction for 20-30% overhead.
stance_target: The repo's assumption that full activation checkpointing at 32k is affordable on a compute-rich, memory-poor box
quoted_support: Full Checkpointing : Checkpoint every layer. Maximum memory savings (~linear in number of layers), maximum compute cost (~30-40% overhead).

claim: CPU offloading of parameters and optimizer state costs 30-50% slowdown for FSDP full offload and 10-20% for ZeRO-2 gradient offload, which matters because the box has 251 GB of DDR4 to trade against 64 GB of HBM per card.
stance_target: Whether host-RAM offload is a viable alternative to freezing Engram tables for fitting 7B on 64 GB cards
scope_conditions: ZeRO-Offload and FSDP CPUOffload; measured slowdown ranges reported without citation
quoted_support: Full CPU offloading provides maximum memory savings at significant performance cost (typically 30-50% slower).
